shorts.title: The Birds on a Buffalo's Back Sometimes Drink Its Blood
shorts.outro: Doug's six deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: Oxpeckers pick ticks off Cape buffalo, but they also eat earwax and wound tissue and are known to drink blood, and in a Zimbabwe study cattle wounds healed faster without them. The science is real and sourced in the full video.

shorts.hook: A buffalo herd decides where to go next by holding a vote.
shorts.title: Buffalo Herds Vote on Where to Go. Doug Voted Wrong
shorts.outro: Doug's other five deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: Ecologist Herbert Prins watched cows in a herd of almost a thousand Cape buffalo at Lake Manyara pick the evening direction by standing and staring, a habit a Nature review called voting. Doug's cartoon death and his other five are in the full video.

shorts.hook: Lions caught a buffalo calf. Then the herd came back.
shorts.title: Lions Caught a Buffalo Calf. Then the Herd Came Back
shorts.outro: Doug's six deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: In 2004 at Kruger National Park, tourists filmed lions catching a buffalo calf, a crocodile joining in, and the herd coming back to win it free. Doug stayed in the car for once; his six cartoon deaths are in the full video.
